paragraphs: AWE Learning sells self-contained childrens learning workstations to public libraries and community organizations across the United States and Canada, aimed at learners ages 2 to 12. The stations arrive turnkey, meant to support school readiness and early literacy and to extend programming without adding staff time.

The current release, Platinum Version 4 of the Early Literacy Station and AfterSchool Edge, carries more than 250 titles and runs without an internet connection or ads. Modules span literacy, math, STEM, and creativity. Rather than tap-and-swipe alone, each station combines touchscreen, mouse, and keyboard so children practice navigation, coordination, and early typing. The environment is closed and child-safe, built around structured, play-based learning children can work through on their own.

The company was founded in the mid-1990s as a remote network technology company. Work with the Free Library of Philadelphia exposed how hard it was for libraries to manage educational software for young patrons, and the Early Literacy Station grew out of that. It says its products are used by over 49% of U.S. public libraries. More than 40,000 workstations have been sold, according to the same page. AWE Learning is headquartered in Chester, Pennsylvania, with account executives across North America.

quote.text: Every child deserves access to high-quality learning tools, regardless of background or resources.
